newsitem.title: KENYA: Alleged Sudan coup plotters on trial, rights group.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Sudan coup plotters on trial, rights group.

text.p: A Sudanese military tribunal is conducting a secret trial of 21 alleged coup plotters in Khartoum, a New York-based human rights group said on Friday.

In a letter to Sudanese President Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir, Human Rights Watch said the trial, widespread arrests by security agents and reported torture reflected how the human rights situation had worsened in the last few months.
It said the accused, known as "the Port Sudan defendants", included 10 civilians, seven of whom were never in the military, and they went on trial at military intelligence headquarters this month.
Human Rights Watch said the procedures in the secret trial made "a mockery of justice" as the defendants had no rights to defence lawyers in a tribunal that was not legally qualified.
It said before last year most similar trials of alleged coup plotters took place in civilian courts except for the execution of 28 military officers in 1990 following a summary trial.
Human Rights Watch said Bashir's government was apparently relying on secret military tribunals because convictions and heavier sentences were more likely than in civilian courts.

It said it was concerned at the lack of a fair trial for Colonel Awad Alkarim Elnaga and others on trial since last year and a large numbers of detentions by Sudanese security agents in recent months.
"We are particularly alarmed many detainees have been and/or are being held in secret unacknowledged detention facilities known as 'ghost houses' where they reportedly are tortured," it added.
"We are well aware of military developments inside Sudan and of your government's accusations against neighbouring countries, and their's against you," it told Bashir in its letter to him.
"Nevertheless the need for military defence is no justification for any of the parties to ride roughshod over basic human rights," it added.
Sudan has accused Eritrean and Ethiopian troops of invading its territory last month in support of a rebel offensive in the east. Both countries have denied the charges by Khartoum.
